result.title: Trust Test for Agentic AI
result.description:
AI is moving beyond tools that respond to human instruction towards systems capable of acting with greater autonomy. As agentic AI enters public services and business operations, it could significantly expand human capability and value creation but only if its actions can be governed in ways that preserve accountability, judgment and trust.

How do we build trust and governance frameworks that allow agentic AI to move from promise to value while preserving human judgment?


 
Speakers: Yalda Aoukar, Lubna Bouza, Mark-Alexandre Doumba, Omar Sultan Al Olama

result.title: Betazone: The Human-Machine Line
result.description:
Humanoid robots are moving from the demo stage to the shop floor, evolving from curiosities into potential co-workers able to move, sense and decide alongside us.

What would it take for a humanoid to become a genuine collaborator rather than simply another machine?

Join roboticist and designer Madeline Gannon for a visual journey into the emerging world of human-machine collaboration.


 
Speakers: Ambarish Mitra, Dana Alomar, Madeline Gannon

result.title: The world really is more unpredictable than ever - two ‘chief risk officers’ explain why
result.description:
You're not imagining it: the world really is more unpredictable than it used to be. That's the opinion of the chief risk officers at carmaker Volkswagen and the World Trade Organisation, who joined us on Radio Davos to discuss how we can best confront the ever more complex risk landscape.
Geopolitics, supply chains, disinformation and artificial intelligence are among the headline risks that are increasingly interlinked and therefore harder to predict, the risk officers say - but they are both optimistic about our ability to cope.
This episode was recorded live on Thursday, 8 October in front of an online audience as part of the World Economic Forum’s Strategic Intelligence programme of content available exclusively to Forum partners and digital members.

result.title: Economics after Certainty
result.description:
Economic policy-making has long relied on models that promise predictability. Yet repeated shocks, from inflation and financial crises to geopolitical fragmentation, have exposed the limits of forecasts and equilibrium thinking. 

As uncertainty becomes a defining condition, what would a more adaptive approach to economics look like, one that helps economies anticipate change, unlock new sources of growth and strengthen resilience?


 
Speakers: Abeer Abu Omar, Hamed Ali, Chinwe Egwim, Sergei Guriev, Ma Song, Milojko Spajić

result.title: Fair by Design
result.description:
Boardrooms have committed, targets have been set and yet progress has stalled. Women’s share of senior leadership has slipped back, while AI is increasingly shaping how organizations hire, promote and reward, creating both a risk of reproducing existing inequities and an opportunity to redesign how work works.

From rethinking how roles are scoped to embedding fairness into the technologies shaping tomorrow’s workforce, what approaches hold the greatest promise to make fairness the default of work?


 
Speakers: Huda Al Hashimi, Mina Al-Oraibi, Kelsi Doran, Sara Minkara
